text:
Jackson LaCombe has become Anaheim's do-everything defenseman: 27:21 a night, up three minutes from last season, on the ice for 81% of the power play, and a ten-game point streak built entirely on assists (16 of them). He has 22 points in 18 games with only one goal.

This one comes with a warning label. The Ducks have scored 11.1 more goals than the chances deserve while he is on the ice, and at five-on-five they get just 38% of the expected goals with him out there. His scoring rate is far above what our talent range expects from a defenseman of his profile. Some of those assists are teammates finishing at an unsustainable clip.

The skills underneath are real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile of defensemen in primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey had his team creating plenty more with him on. Our projection still says about 81 points. We'd bet on the minutes holding long before we'd bet on the finishing around him.
headline: LaCombe's 27 minutes and a lot of good luck
